query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy provides a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor integrity and tends to crack. Prior studies on related MM′X materials used epoxy-containing Mn0.98CoGe, obtaining compressive strengths of 152 and 218 MPa at two epoxy contents, and low-melting In composites, obtaining 48 MPa compressive strength and more than eight times the thermal conductivity of epoxy-containing samples under the reported conditions. These routes demonstrated gains in selected strength or heat-transport metrics, but the desired coexistence of robust integrity and high caloric performance remains unresolved. The target should also remain rare-earth-free. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing caloric response? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, quantitative or directional outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, boundary conditions under applied-field, pressure, temperature, and loading regimes, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive controlled experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Microalloying the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy caloric alloy with 0.3 at% boron will segregate B to grain boundaries, refine grains, block crack propagation, and double its compressive strength while leaving its magneto- and baro-caloric entropy changes essentially unchanged.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy, 20–50 µm grains, pervasive microcracks, compressive strength <100 MPa, magnetocaloric ΔS_m≈6 J kg⁻¹K⁻¹ under 3 T, barocaloric ΔS_p≈4 J kg⁻¹K⁻¹ under 200 MPa.
generation.intervention: Add 0.3 at% B during melting and casting, followed by homogenization at 900 °C for 24 h under Ar.
generation.conditions: Testing at 300 K±5 K; uniaxial compression at 10⁻³ s⁻¹; magnetic fields up to 3 T; hydrostatic pressures up to 200 MPa.
generation.structural_mediator: B segregated at grain boundaries causing boundary pinning and grain refinement to ~5–10 µm.
generation.mechanism: B atoms segregate to grain boundaries, impede grain growth and crack initiation, increase fracture toughness and strength, while at low concentration they do not appreciably shift the martensitic transformation or magnetic ordering that drive the caloric effects.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compressive strength rises by 50–100% (to ~150–200 MPa); grain size falls to ~5–10 µm; thermal conductivity increases by ~10%; ΔS_m retained within 95% of baseline; ΔS_p within 90% of baseline.
generation.baseline: Compressive strength <100 MPa; ΔS_m≈6 J kg⁻¹K⁻¹; ΔS_p≈4 J kg⁻¹K⁻¹.
generation.boundary: Magnetic field ≤3 T; pressure ≤200 MPa; T=300±5 K; strain rate ≤10⁻³ s⁻¹.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate—B’s effect on the FeCoGe-MnNiSi phase equilibrium is untested; actual entropy-change shift may be up to ~10%.

falsification_experiment.design: Cast two batches of (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38, one with 0.3 at% B and one without. Homogenize both at 900 °C×24 h. Use SEM to measure grain size and crack density. Perform uniaxial compression (10⁻³ s⁻¹) at 300 K to obtain strength. Measure ΔS_m under 3 T via quasi-adiabatic calorimetry and ΔS_p under 200 MPa in a pressure cell.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If B-doped alloy does not exhibit ≥20% higher compressive strength than control or shows >10% reduction in either ΔS_m or ΔS_p, then the hypothesis is falsified.
